extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, NIH peer reviewers, Scientific Review Group members, and NIH staff managing peer review
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural guidance used by NIH Scientific Review Groups and advisory councils to evaluate, score, and make funding recommendations on research and training grant applications. Covers criteria, scoring procedures, human-subjects/inclusion requirements, conflict-of-interest rules, and related oversight documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the initial peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial peer review is to evaluate and rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review is conducted by Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs) housed in NIH Institutes and Centers; examples include the Center for Scientific Review and IC Review Branches for RFAs and special programs. This evaluation forms the basis for further advisory council review and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-step peer review process (SRGs then National Advisory Councils)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of NIH applications takes place in multiple steps: an initial review in SRGs followed by a second level of review by NIH National Advisory Councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Advisory Councils composed of extramural scientists and public representatives provide cross-sectional advice during deliberation and decisions. SRG outcomes and council deliberations together inform funding actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosters of Scientific Review Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership rosters for standing review committees and Special Emphasis Panels are maintained and made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rosters provide transparency about who is reviewing applications and can be used to understand reviewer expertise and potential conflicts; CSR website contains additional roster information and related referral/peer review resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Advisory Committee (PRAC) oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: PRAC provides advisory oversight on NIH peer review practices and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRAC resources and pages provide deliberations, recommendations, and historical context for peer review policy development and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: General expectations and procedures for reviewers participating in NIH peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines outline reviewer responsibilities, evaluation conduct, scoring, confidentiality, and administrative processes; see linked guideline documents for specific reviewer instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Procedures for Scientific Review Group Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules and expectations for conduct of SRG meetings where initial peer review takes place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers meeting preparation, discussion format, assignment of reviewers, handling of applications, voting/scoring processes, and documentation. Details are provided in SRG procedure documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications (NOT-OD-05-002)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced updated, explicit statements of review criteria for evaluating research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes a comparison of updated versus previous criteria and a Questions & Answers document to clarify how the new criteria should be applied in reviews; linked MS Word documents provide the text of the updated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of updated and previous criteria for evaluating applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A document comparing the new explicit review criteria with the prior criteria to help reviewers and applicants understand changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides side-by-side comparisons and explanatory notes; useful for reviewers learning the updated framework and for applicants revising submissions to meet new expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Scientific Review's procedures for scoring applications during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies numerical scoring scales, how summary scores are computed, and how scorers should assign values based on criterion evaluations; referenced in CSR scoring procedure document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures intended to increase efficiency of review for certain application types while maintaining quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined review may modify discussion/assignment practices for applications deemed non-competitive or clear cases; the specific implementation details are provided in the Streamlined Review guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Review of Specific Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental guidance tailored to review of particular types of applications (e.g., RFAs, program projects, clinical research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains special considerations, altered scoring emphases, or procedural variations that apply to those specific application mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of New Investigator R01s
rubrics_metrics.description: Special review guidance addressing evaluation of R01 applications from new investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides considerations to ensure fairness to new investigators, such as weighing potential and career stage appropriately; resources for new investigators are linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Research Involving Natural Products (complex mixtures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reviewing research involving natural products that are prepared as complex mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses unique methodological, characterization, and reproducibility concerns for complex mixtures and how reviewers should evaluate scientific rigor and feasibility in such studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Grant Application and Award procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Format-specific guidance for modular budget applications and their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how modular applications present budgets and how budget assessment interacts with scientific review; procedural notes for reviewers on assessing resources within the modular format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest, Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure rules for NIH peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and non-disclosure that apply to NIH peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes information for reviewers of grant applications and R&D contract proposals, pre- and post-review certification forms, and links to the OER Conflict of Interest page. Documents specify what constitutes a conflict, required recusal behaviors, and confidentiality obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Pre-Review and Post-Review Certification Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative certification forms reviewers must complete before and after participating in review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to document conflict-of-interest disclosures, confidentiality commitments, and adherence to reviewer responsibilities; PDFs and Word versions are provided for reviewer completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH instructions for evaluating research involving human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for reviewers on how to evaluate human-subjects protections and related ethics in grant and cooperative agreement applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers required components (e.g., IRB, informed consent, risk minimization), criteria for sufficiency of protections, and interaction with inclusion policies; linked PDF provides detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for human and animal subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices and requirements applicants must satisfy regarding human and animal subjects in funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important applicant notices outline regulatory and policy requirements, documentation expectations, and consequences for non-compliance; reviewers are directed to consider these requirements during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Decision Trees for human subject protection and inclusion issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision trees to guide reviewers and administrators when assessing human subject protection and participant inclusion concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides stepwise procedures for identifying problems and determining appropriate review or administrative actions; supports consistent handling of inclusion and protection issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects and Inclusion Policies (Women, Minorities, Children)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and guidance concerning protection of human participants and requirements for inclusion of women, minorities, and children in clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes PowerPoint/PDF resources on protection, inclusion in Phase III trials, and subgroup considerations; reviewers are expected to evaluate adequacy of inclusion plans and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and guidance for evaluating data and safety monitoring plans proposed for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when monitoring plans are required, acceptable monitoring strategies, and how reviewers should judge whether proposed monitoring appropriately protects participants and study integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating of Grant Applications — explicit statements of review criteria (1997 update and related deliberations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official statements and deliberations establishing explicit review criteria used to rate grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and oversight group reports (PROG) and NIH announcements explain the rationale and implementation of explicit review criteria; reviewers should apply these standardized criteria when assigning merit ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Initial Scientific Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for applicants to appeal initial peer review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the appeals process, grounds for appeal, and administrative handling; both applicants and reviewers should be aware of appeal pathways and documentation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Regulations (42 CFR Part 52h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulations governing the scientific peer review of research grant applications and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Rules and Federal Register notices codify statutory/regulatory requirements for peer review practice; reviewers and administrators must comply with these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Notes and historical deliberations (PROG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and records (e.g., CSR Peer Review Notes, PROG deliberations) documenting developments, policy changes, and oversight findings relevant to peer review practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents provide context, examples of policy implementation, and historical lessons to inform current reviewer behavior and policy interpretation.
